finding.summary: The issue's literal acceptance scenario (D1–D5 formulas in one sheet) is not demonstrated and likely does not produce the stated numbers, because expansion uses whole-sheet used bounds
finding.evidence: The issue fixes a single setup (A1=10,A2=20,A3=30,B1=100,B2=200) and expects D1..D5 to yield 60/110/200/5/360 simultaneously. `resolveRange` fills omitted columns from `Store.getUsedBounds()`, which is the bounding box of *all* populated cells including the D-column formula cells. With all five formulas present, `=SUM(1:1)` in D2 expands to `A1:D1` (D1 = 60) → 170, and `=SUM(1:3)` in D5 expands to `A1:D3` → 360 + D1 + D2 + D3. packages/sheets/test/sheet/calculation.test.ts sidesteps this by constructing `new Sheet(new MemStore())` per case and placing only one formula. Related unspecified case: a whole-column formula placed *inside* the referenced column (e.g. `=SUM(A:A)` in A5) becomes self-referential once bounds include the formula cell — neither the design doc nor the tests state the intended behavior (Excel raises a circular-reference error).
